name: Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi energy function: Gamma^2 = 1 + 2E; E > 0 unbound (hyperbolic) shell

source.located: Lemaitre 1933 (Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles A 53, 51; GRG 29, 637 (1997) transl.), Tolman 1934 (PNAS 20, 169), Bondi 1947 (MNRAS 107, 410) -- no arXiv copies. Read via restatement: (i) Bolejko, Celerier & Krasinski, 'Inhomogeneous cosmological models: exact solutions and their applications', CQG 28, 164002 (2011), arXiv:1102.1449v2: eq.(15) ds^2 = dt^2 - R_r^2/(1+2E) dr^2 - R^2 dOmega^2; eq.(16) R_t^2 = 2E + 2M/R + Lambda R^2/3; p.4 'The sign of k(r) determines the type of evolution when Lambda = 0; with k > 0 = Lambda the model expands ... and then recollapses ...; with k < 0 = Lambda the model is either ever-expanding or ever-collapsing; k = 0 = Lambda is the intermediate case' with (-k, Phi) -> (2E, R) (p.6); eq.(11) the pressure (Lemaitre-model) form e^B = R_r^2/(1+2E(r)) exp(int 2 R_t p_r / ((rho+p) R_r) dt). (ii) Lasky, Lun & Burston, arXiv gr-qc/0606003 eq.(29)-(30) (convention 1+E), p.9 'E(R), arbitrary up to the constraint E(R) > -1, is a measure of the energy of a shell', fn.2 p.13 'E(R) < 0 is the bound case and E(R) > 0 is the unbound case'. (iii) Lasky & Lun, PRD 74, 084013 (2006), arXiv gr-qc/0606055: eq.(27) (1/(1+E)) L_n E = 2 sqrt(2M/r+E) P'/(rho+P) -- E(t,r) not conserved with pressure gradients; eq.(40)-(42); p.5 'the cases of E being positive, negative or equivalently zero correspond to unbound, bound and marginally bound models'.

published_statement: Bolejko-Celerier-Krasinski (1102.1449) eqs.(15)-(16): for dust (p = 0, so A_r = 0 and g_00 scaled to 1) the Lemaitre-Tolman metric is ds^2 = dt^2 - R_r^2/(1+2E(r)) dr^2 - R^2 dOmega^2 with R_t^2 = 2E + 2M/R + (Lambda/3) R^2, E(r) and M(r) arbitrary; 'Because the pressure is zero, the mass does not depend on time.' Evolution type (p.4 with (-k,Phi)->(2E,R)): 'when Lambda = 0', E < 0 recollapses (elliptic, bound), E > 0 is ever-expanding or ever-collapsing (hyperbolic, unbound), E = 0 intermediate (parabolic, marginally bound). Lasky-Lun-Burston fn.2: 'E(R) < 0 is the bound case and E(R) > 0 is the unbound case'; E > -1 (their 1+E convention) for Lorentzian signature. Hence Gamma := e^{-Lambda_metric} R' = sqrt(1+2E) and Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E is the LTB statement the tree quotes.
published_hypotheses: dust: perfect fluid with p = 0 (Bolejko et al. p.2 'The matter source in them is dust'; eq.(15) derived 'When p_,r = 0')
comoving, geodesic flow (lapse = 1; Lasky-Lun-Burston eq.(11)-(12): 'the dust particles are moving along timelike geodesics ... a result of there being zero pressure')
no radial energy flux (G_tr = 0 in comoving coordinates; re-derived C1a)

Lambda = 0 for the sign-of-E classification of bound / marginal / unbound evolution (Bolejko et al. p.4 'when Lambda = 0'); with Lambda the threshold moves (Le Delliou-Mena-Mimoso 0911.0241 eq.(15): E_lim = -(3M)^{2/3} Lambda^{1/3}, their E = 2E here)
1 + 2E > 0 (Lorentzian signature; Lasky-Lun-Burston p.9 'E(R) > -1' in the 1+E convention)
R' > 0 away from necks/shell crossings (so e^{Lambda} = R'/sqrt(1+2E) with the positive root)
normalisation convention g_rr = R'^2/(1+2E) (Bondi/Bolejko-Krasinski); Lasky-Lun and Le Delliou et al. write 1+E, so 'twice' is convention-bound

Re-derived (C3b): D_t Gamma = U D_r Phi - (R/2) e^{-Phi-Lam} G_tr, the same structure as the owner's own driven.py:240 'D_t Gamma = 4 pi R j + U D_r Phi'; so D_t E = Gamma D_t Gamma != 0 unless D_r Phi = 0 (perfect fluid: p' = 0) and there is no flux -- agreeing with Lasky-Lun gr-qc/0606055 eq.(27) and Bolejko et al. eq.(11). Counterexample (C7): Minkowski (m = 0), shells R = r0 + A sin T, A = 0.5: E = U^2/2 > 0 at almost every instant while every shell stays in [r0 - A, r0 + A] forever. So outside geodesic flow E > 0 is an instantaneous label, not unboundedness. The owners' V9 (driven.py:596-601) fixes the 1+2E convention explicitly, so the statement is internally consistent.

lacked_data: The classic authors lacked a measured Lambda: Lemaitre (1933) carried Lambda as a parameter, and the sign-of-E classification is quoted at Lambda = 0 (1102.1449 p.4). Lambda > 0 was measured later (Planck 2018: Lambda = 1.089e-52 m^-2). Having it DOES change the classification in principle -- E > 0 is no longer necessary for unboundedness, and the threshold becomes 2E_lim = -(3M)^{2/3}Lambda^{1/3} (C5, 0911.0241 eq.15) -- but the computed window is 1.29e-15 in 2E for a solar mass and 2.7e-19 for an Earth mass, so no reading the board makes moves, and the H0 tension moves that window by only 6.5 %. The identity Gamma^2 - 1 = 2E needs no data and is untouched. The limit that matters is not missing data but a hypothesis: the unbound reading needs dust (geodesic, p' = 0, no flux) flow, and the counterexample C7 shows that off geodesic flow E > 0 does not mean unbound. Evidence against M's hypothesis here: the 1930s-1940s result is a definition plus a dust orbit classification, both exact on their stated class and re-derived here; nothing in it is inaccurate, and the one datum that arrived later (Lambda) moves it only by a computed negligible amount.
grade_evidence: The identity the tree quotes STANDS: Gamma^2 = 1 + 2E on the LTB metric (C1b; owner V9 residual 0 re-run), Misner-Sharp form Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2m/R (C1c), FRW E = -k r^2/2 for any a(t) (C2), and at Lambda = 0 for dust E > 0 <=> unbound for every sign of M (C4, z3). The tree uses the unbound (hyperbolic) reading on a larger class than the source: (1) Lambda = 0 is dropped (driven.py:78-80, 215-217, 398-401; drivensource.py:183-186) -- with Lambda != 0 E > 0 is neither necessary nor sufficient for unbound (C5, z3 witness; 0911.0241 eq.15), though C6 computes the effect as negligible at the board's scales; (2) dust / geodesic / no-flux flow is dropped (drivensource.py:186 'THE CONFIGURATION IS UNBOUND'; driven.py:80 'Contraction IS unboundedness') -- D_t E = Gamma D_t Gamma != 0 off that class (C3, matching the owner's own driven.py:240 and Lasky-Lun eq.27), and the Minkowski oscillating-shell family (C7) has E > 0 at almost every instant while bounded forever. Not WRONG: on the tree's own witnesses (open FRW, Milne, PG/Lemaitre slicing -- all geodesic, Lambda = 0) the reading is exact, and nothing the board refuses rests on it (rests_on_it = a tautological selftest fixture and a STANDARD-table label; the anchor lemma and the displacement bound use Gamma and m, not the unbound reading). The float discrepancy in contraction_is_unbound is an owner-code discrepancy, not a property of the external result.
what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS if the owners' unbound/hyperbolic reading were scoped to geodesic (p' = 0, no-flux) comoving flow with Lambda = 0 -- e.g. driven.py:80 and drivensource.py:186 carrying 'LTB/dust, Lambda = 0' as named hypotheses -- or restated as the label 'E > 0' with the fate claim removed. WRONG only if some tree conclusion were shown to depend on reading E > 0 as an asymptotic fate for non-geodesic flow (none found: rests_on_it lists only the tautological fixture and the table label). OPEN would require the restatement sources to disagree with the pre-arXiv originals, which cannot be checked here.
